solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Restore theatre publicity

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
to give something an airing, or air, is to publicise it

explanation.surface: A call to bring back the old way of promoting plays.
explanation.walkthrough: REP (repertory theatre, a company staging a changing programme of plays) plus AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore a broken thing is to mend it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Coal not needing starter to burn

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, which is not needed here, so the opening letter of the coal type goes

parts.note: lignite is a soft brown coal

explanation.surface: Some coal catches fire without anything to start it.
explanation.walkthrough: LIGNITE (brown coal) loses its first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To set alight or catch fire; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Broadcast of cricket test is on, clever clogs

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering seed widely, so the letters of the following words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Coverage of a cricket Test match is on air, a know-all observes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like television coverage of the match; it is the anagram signal for CRICKET TEST IS ON. Clever clogs is British slang for a show-off who is too clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a genius or know-all, from the phrase that a hard task is no job for a brainbox.

clue.text: Sailors' song overheard — coarse stuff

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: sailors are a crew and a song is a ditty, giving crew ditty

explanation.surface: A shanty sung on board is overheard and found to be vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarseness or vulgarity in speech or art, such as a rude shanty contains.

clue.text: Stone worker's design of sun and moon interrupted by intellectual old woman

definitions.note: read as 'stone worker is', the apostrophe s being a contraction of is

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are broken into by the following pieces, which sit within them
a design arranges things in a pattern, so the letters of the two heavenly bodies are rearranged

parts.note: mental means relating to the mind or intellect
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A sculptor's sun-and-moon motif is spoilt by a bluestocking matron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design of' is the anagram signal, and 'interrupted by' puts the two pieces into the middle of the shuffled letters. The 's of 'worker's' reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who carves gravestones and memorials is the trade name for a stone worker of this kind.

clue.text: Ready with treatment, coming in to block imaginary abstraction

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come into the middle of the barrier word

parts.note: a dam blocks a river

indicators.note: letters given treatment are worked over and reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: Someone prepared for therapy finds it stops their fanciful brooding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with treatment' rearranges READY into AYDREA, which goes 'coming in to' DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a state of abstraction full of fancies, so it is an imagined absent-mindedness.

clue.text: Running about last no source of achievement? It's not everything

indicators.note: running water moves freely, so the letters here are set loose into a new order
no says the letter that follows is lacking from the words before
the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A runner coming last achieves nothing, but placing isn't everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no source of achievement' removes A from ABOUT LAST, leaving BOUTLST, which 'Running' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial sum is a figure short of the full amount, so it is not the whole lot.

clue.text: Negligée half-open, lingerie uncovered, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the gathered letters could be arranged in another way
only half of the word open is kept, its first two letters
with its covers off, the word loses its outer letters, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: A negligée hangs half-open, the lingerie beneath on show.
explanation.walkthrough: OP (half of OPEN) and INGERI (LINGERIE without its ends) are rearranged, 'possibly' being the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose dressing gown for women, the French-named garment is a kind of negligée.

clue.text: Past question posed in Old English is unclear

indicators.note: posed means placed, so the pieces are set within the outer letters

parts.note: PA is a short form of past, as in past tense

explanation.surface: A historic question asked in Anglo-Saxon remains obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one cannot see through, or a hard-to-follow text, is unclear.

clue.text: Lament dropping second vase

indicators.note: dropping says a piece is let fall from the word for lament

parts.note: to mourn is to lament
mo is an informal word for a moment or second

explanation.surface: Mourning someone after a vase is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall rounded vessel, often for ashes, is a kind of vase.

clue.text: Father, getting cut, acted rashly

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
nicked means cut slightly

explanation.surface: Dad nicks himself shaving and loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's nerve and behaving without thought is acting rashly.

clue.text: Put new software on mobile device in truck

indicators.note: in places the handheld device inside the vehicle word

parts.note: ute is short for utility vehicle, an Australian pickup truck
a PDA is a personal digital assistant, a handheld computer

explanation.surface: A tradesman installing software on a handheld left in a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Installing a newer version of a program is the standard computing sense of refreshing it.

clue.text: Like savage warrior in bad dream as experienced by nippers?

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of dream are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: nippers are teeth, so what they experience happens 'to the teeth'

explanation.surface: A nightmare of a fierce fighter, as children might picture it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nippers' looks like children; here it means teeth. 'bad' rearranges DREAM into ARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being heavily equipped with weapons, as a fearsome fighter is.

clue.text: South-eastern resort dismissing crowd damage

indicators.note: dismissing sends away the crowd word from the town's name

parts.note: Margate is a seaside resort in Kent, south-east England
a gate is the crowd attending a sports match

explanation.surface: A seaside town turning away visitors and harming itself.
explanation.walkthrough: GATE is British for a sports crowd, or its size.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or impair something is to damage it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Fail to appear for an informal event

definitions.meaning: to withdraw from a race or match, so not turning up
a ... match or team is one got up informally at short notice

explanation.surface: Failing to show up for a casual get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the same word: withdrawing an entrant, and an impromptu, makeshift gathering.

clue.text: Cracked up about new acceptable flavouring

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word goes round the letter for new
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: cracked means crazy, as is manic
'not on' means unacceptable, so on means acceptable

explanation.surface: A crazy cook is gushing about a novel, fine spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MANIC into CINAM, which goes 'about' N to make CINNAM, then ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice from tree bark, it is used to flavour cakes and curries.

clue.text: Who'll produce moving art in a mo?

definitions.text: Who'll produce moving art in a mo?

indicators.note: moving letters are shifted around into a different order

explanation.surface: Asking who can make a cartoon in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges ART IN A MO, and the whole clue also defines: a creator of moving pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon maker produces moving pictures, art that moves on screen.

clue.text: Second glass not filled? That's a slip

indicators.note: a glass that is not filled is short of full, so the last letter is missing

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass

explanation.surface: Pouring a second drink short could be a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip or slip is a misstep, either on foot or in speech.

clue.text: Supposedly vital measurement that's incomplete for vehicle

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: bust is one of a figure's 'vital statistics', with waist and hips

explanation.surface: A tape measure failing to go round enough for a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital statistics' is the old British phrase for a woman's bust, waist and hip measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: A large public road vehicle carrying passengers is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Box left in a mess? Utterly

indicators.note: in puts the container and the letter for left inside the mess

parts.note: a sty is a filthy, messy place
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A box left lying in a mess, completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'stark naked', the adverb means completely or utterly.

clue.text: What allows some air into a dramatic stand-off?

definitions.text: What allows some air into a dramatic stand-off?

parts.words: What allows some air into a dramatic stand-off?
parts.note: air is a tune, and a play's tense pause is filled with background tunes written for the stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like ventilation and 'stand-off' a confrontation; the air is a melody and the drama a theatre play.
explanation.definitionFit: Background tunes accompanying a stage play are written to fill such moments.

clue.text: Province seeing governor not initially going round street

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the street abbreviation
not initially means without the letter it starts with

parts.note: a ruler governs

explanation.surface: A province where the governor goes round the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: ULSTER is one of Ireland's four historic provinces, its name often used for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic division of Ireland, it is one of that island's four provinces.

clue.text: l? I'd turned up amongst singles

definitions.note: the symbol I, printed here as a lowercase-looking l, stands for one chemical element

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: I and one are both single units

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a letter turned up among single items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amongst' places DI (I'D reversed by 'turned up') between IO and NE of I ONE. The definition is the chemical symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: The element with chemical symbol I is the antiseptic halogen element.

clue.text: Nested containers requiring filling?

indicators.note: nested containers sit one inside another

parts.note: a vat and a can are both containers
a can, like a tin, is a container, the second vessel the word supplies

explanation.surface: Stacked boxes that are waiting to be packed.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'containers' does double duty here, supplying two different vessels, one sitting inside the other as 'Nested' says.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty post or seat is one waiting to be filled.

clue.text: Emotional piece audibly criticises leaderless group

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so a word with the same sound is written

parts.note: raps means criticises sharply

indicators.note: without its leader, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a body is a group of people

explanation.surface: A passionate composition is loudly slated by a band without a frontman.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-form musical work of intense feeling, like Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue.

clue.text: What newspapers rely on: scandal seeing religious figure ousted

indicators.note: ousted means thrown out, so the saint's letters go

parts.note: a stink is a public fuss or scandal
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Tabloids depending on a scandal involving a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scandal' looks like what papers rely on; the definition is the printing fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint needs it for printing; papers rely on this fluid to put words on the page.

clue.text: Likely to leak old Russian's first work about America

indicators.note: about turns the first group of letters round
first takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
US is short for United States

explanation.surface: A defector: an old Russian's first work on America is leaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the first three pieces round together, giving PORO; only then does the country come after.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of tiny holes, so liable to let water or air through.

clue.text: Edit one does after climax of novel — to resolve this?

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters come behind the letter from the novel
the climax of a story comes at the end, so the final letter
editing reworks the letters into another order

explanation.surface: An editor tidying a novel's ending ties up the dangling threads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edit' rearranges ONE DOES, which comes 'after' L, the last letter of 'novel'. 'this' is what an editor resolves.
explanation.definitionFit: An unresolved detail or thread in a plot is what an editor ties up.
